# Daily Macro Digest — 5 August 2026

## The 24-Hour Story

A confusing, cross-current day: oil dropped sharply on signs of Iran diplomatic progress, yet gold and silver surged as if the world were getting riskier, not calmer. This is unusual because the Hormuz-tension relationship (#1 in our framework) would normally push oil and gold in the *same* direction. Instead, headlines suggest oil fell on "peace deal" optimism (crude inventory builds, US/Qatar signalling progress on an Iran draft deal) even while other reports flagged escalating Hormuz tanker attacks and stalled traffic — genuinely mixed signals from the same region. Gold's rally looks driven more by the falling US 10Y yield (lower real yields make non-yielding gold relatively more attractive — relationship #8) than by oil-driven inflation fears. Separately, weak China iron ore demand data (a one-year low) didn't stop ASX materials from rising 1.25% — a disconnect worth noting rather than explaining away. AUD/USD and the USD Index were both roughly flat, and VIX rose modestly but isn't flagged as unusual.

## Flagged Assets

**Gold (+2.48%, unusual move)** — Likely supported by the drop in US 10Y yields (lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold). In 2 past episodes of a similar-sized gold jump, the metal was up a further 3.55% and 0.37% cumulatively over the following days — a small sample, so treat as context only, not a pattern.

**Silver (+3.64%, unusual move)** — Silver's larger percentage jump than gold nudges the gold/silver ratio down, which per relationship #2 can suggest an industrial-demand or growth story rather than pure fear — though that sits oddly against weak China iron ore data reported today. Only 1 past episode on record (up 3.99% then +2.96% cumulative over following days) — too small a sample to draw any conclusion.

**WTI Crude (-6.34%, unusual move)** — Headlines directly explain this: US crude inventory builds plus US/Qatar signalling progress on an Iran draft deal reduced the supply-risk premium. Note one headline warns "markets price in an Iran deal that does not exist yet" — the drop may be running ahead of confirmed facts. Only 1 past similar episode (-8.21%, then +9.02% cumulative over following days) — sample too small to mean much.

**US 10Y Yield (-1.26%, unusual move)** — No clear headline driver in today's feed (rates/economic-indicator sources returned errors). Only 1 past episode recorded, insufficient for pattern reading.

## What to Watch

- Whether the Iran/Hormuz situation resolves toward genuine de-escalation or further attacks — today's headlines contradict each other (traffic stalling vs. deal progress), so oil's next move is uncertain.
- China demand data follow-through: iron ore at a one-year low is a relationship-#4 warning sign for AUD and ASX materials, even though materials rose today.
- Any confirmation (or denial) of the reported Iran draft deal, which is currently priced into oil but not yet confirmed.

*Informational only — not a trading signal.*
